sheet-23-1.description: The main part of sheet 23 covers the Kearny side of the Harrison town line between Schuyler Avenue and Sandford Avenue, from the Newark and Paterson Branch of the Erie Railroad near the top down to Harrison Avenue at the bottom, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north nearly straight up. The town line between Harrison and Kearny runs down Schuyler Avenue, marked by a dash-dot line with the lettering Town of Harrison and Town of Kearny. Radley Street crosses the part about two thirds of the way down; Hamilton Street meets Schuyler Avenue from the Harrison side just above it, and Watkins Street and Franklyn Street are lettered at the top, north of the railroad. The blocks are cut into narrow house lots, most of them vacant; a scattering of frame dwellings, sheds and a dairy stand along Schuyler Avenue, Sandford Avenue and Radley Street. The only industry is the Harrison Pickle and Vinegar Works at the corner of Schuyler Avenue and the railroad, with a shipping and bottling building and an engine and vat room. The lower third, toward Harrison Avenue, is almost empty apart from a saloon at Schuyler Avenue and a few small buildings. Below Harrison Avenue the sheet shows the ends of Sandford Avenue, Greeley Avenue and Boylan Avenue, which continue on sheet 24. Water pipes of 6 and 8 inches, hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked, and a scale of feet is printed at the bottom. Adjoining sheets referenced are 76 at the top, 22 to the west and 15 and 24 below Harrison Avenue.
notes: Sandford Avenue is Sanford Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Watkins Street no longer exists.
The Harrison Pickle and Vinegar Works stands at Schuyler Avenue and the Erie Railroad's Newark and Paterson Branch.
Boylan Avenue's modern junction with Harrison Avenue lies about 16 m from where this sheet draws it and was not used for control.

Harrison Avenue / Schuyler Avenue and Harrison Avenue / Sanford Avenue were hand-picked; the west edge of Sandford Avenue is not drawn near Harrison Avenue, so its centre there was taken 25 ft from the drawn east edge.

Boylan / Harrison drawn about 16 m from its modern node (excluded).

sheet-23-2.description: An inset in the upper right corner of sheet 23, set off by a heavy border and drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left, so that Harrison Avenue runs up the page from west to east. It shows Harrison Avenue in the Kearny meadows east of Boylan Avenue, from Greenfield Avenue, which meets it from the south near the bottom of the inset, to the point where Frank Creek turns along the south side of the avenue at the top. A box at the top of the inset outlines the creek and refers to sheet 25, which continues the avenue eastward over the creek. The south side of Harrison Avenue carries a short row of old frame buildings: a wagon shed, a saloon, sheds and a dwelling, with the note that all these buildings are old and dilapidated, and below Greenfield Avenue a pair of three-story frame buildings. The north side of the avenue is blank. An 8 inch water pipe and hydrants run along Harrison Avenue, and the avenue is lettered as 66 feet wide and Greenfield Avenue as 50 feet. Sheet 24 is referenced south of Greenfield Avenue.
notes: Placed from one detected junction (Greenfield Avenue / Harrison Avenue) with the rotation measured from Harrison Avenue's drawn lines and the atlas scale; low confidence.
Modern parcel lines follow the outline of Frank Creek drawn at the top of the inset.

sheet-24.description: A sparsely built strip of Kearny along the Harrison border, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top and slightly to the right. Harrison Avenue forms the top edge and Greenfield Avenue the right edge, where the sheet meets sheet 23. A wide diagonal band of long narrow lots runs from the upper left to the lower right between Boylan Avenue, Greeley Avenue and Gordon Avenue, almost entirely vacant; the only buildings are a short row of frame dwellings, tenements and sheds on the Boylan Avenue frontage at the top right, and a pickling works with an ice house at the middle left, marked J. B. Morrison, Pickler, with its power, heating and lighting noted as stoves and kerosene. Sandford Avenue runs down the left centre, widening from 35 to 60 feet. West of it, Ann Street, Jersey, Warren, Wilhelm and Sussex streets cross a block of lots to Ogden Avenue, which is the boundary between the Town of Kearny and the Town of Harrison and runs diagonally down the left edge. Only a few coops, dwellings and sheds stand on these lots. A large triangular tract between Gordon Avenue and Sandford Avenue is left blank and numbered 4. The compass rose and scale of feet are drawn on the sheet, and block numbers 15 and 16 mark the Harrison side across Ogden Avenue.
notes: Sandford Avenue is now Sanford Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the modern line is several metres from the drawn one near Ann Street, so that junction was not used.
Greeley Avenue, Gordon Avenue, Jersey, Warren, Wilhelm and Sussex are not in the OpenStreetMap network at these places.
Placed from one hand-picked junction (Boylan Avenue and Greenfield Avenue) at the atlas scale; low confidence.

50 ft. Kearny/Harrison border south of Harrison Av (Greeley, Gordon, Boylan, Sandford, Ann, Jersey, Warren, Wilhelm, Sussex, Ogden); most streets gone; anchored on hand-picked Boylan / Greenfield (north 11). Ann / Sanford displaced about 8 m.

sheet-25.description: A meadow sheet south of Harrison Avenue at Frank Creek, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the top. Harrison Avenue crosses the upper part of the sheet diagonally, rising to the east, with Frank Creek running close along its south side and passing under it by a bridge; the creek also forms the west edge of the drawn area, where it bends south. North of the avenue the area marked 2 belongs to another sheet and is left blank. The sheet is given over to meat packing. The Harrison Branch of Swift and Company of New York (dressed beef and by-products) occupies the centre and south: a wagon shed, a large liming vat room, a reinforced concrete glue manufacturing building still unfinished, an ice machine room, engine and boiler rooms, and a long row of cooler, slaughtering, oil, tankage, tallow and fertilizer buildings, with water tanks of 60,000 gallons and a fire protection note listing watchmen, sprinklers and hose houses. To the east, the Bimbler and Van Wagenen hog slaughter houses (shipping, killing and scalding, drying and hog pens) are joined to Swift's by bridges, and the Newark Stock Yard Company's long live stock pens and feed storage run south from Harrison Avenue. Several railroad sidings curve in from the north across Harrison Avenue to serve the plants. A cable tower stands north of the avenue. A scale of feet is printed at the bottom left.
notes: No street junction on the sheet: placed from one point carried from sheet 23 part 2 (Frank Creek turning along Harrison Avenue), the atlas scale and a north direction of -11 degrees from Harrison Avenue's drawn line against its modern bearing; low confidence.
Modern Bergen Avenue south of Harrison Avenue follows the line of the Newark Stock Yard Company's live stock pens.
Industries: Swift and Company of N.Y. Harrison Branch; Bimbler and Van Wagenen hog slaughter houses; Newark Stock Yard Co.

50 ft, north up. Meadows south of Harrison Av at Frank Creek: Swift & Co. Harrison Branch, Newark Stock Yard Co., Bimbler & Van Wagenen. No street junction; placed from a point carried from sheet 23 part 2 (Frank Creek turning along Harrison Av) with north from Harrison Av; low confidence.

sheet-35.description: A strip of the Kearny and Harrison border district drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper left. Davis Avenue, 70 feet wide, runs down the left edge. From it Tappan Street and Dukes Street run east in parallel, and Prospect Street lies along the bottom of the sheet. The sheet is mostly built up as a street of narrow, deep lots with frame dwellings, many of them two and a half storeys, with sheds, coops and stables to the rear; a few flats and a saloon stand near the Davis Avenue corners, and storage buildings and wagon sheds are scattered along the right edge. The boundary between the Town of Kearny and the Town of Harrison is drawn as a dash-dot line across the lower part of the sheet along Dukes Street, and the vacant block between it and Prospect Street, numbered 60, lies in Harrison. The upper two thirds of the sheet is a large, mostly empty tract of meadow lots numbered 1 with a few scattered dwellings and the compass rose. A pond with its winding outlet, shaded blue, borders the right edge beside Worthington Avenue, and the 6 and 8 inch water pipes are lettered along the streets. Streets of the neighbouring sheet 38 are cut off at the left edge: Pomeroy Avenue, Devon Terrace and Hoyt Street. The header reads Kearny & Harrison, and block numbers 36, 37, 38, 47, 57 and 76 refer to adjoining sheets.
notes: Worthington Avenue north of Harrison Avenue is now Kingsland Avenue.

Pomeroy Avenue, Devon Terrace and Prospect Street have no OpenStreetMap equivalent matched here; the modern Devon Terrace junction with Davis Avenue lies about 12 m from the drawn one, so it was not used.

sheet-36.description: A landscape sheet on the Kearny and Harrison boundary drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the right. The Erie Railroad's Newark and Paterson Branch runs from top to bottom through the middle as a bundle of parallel tracks, with the Harrison Railroad Station, a one storey frame building, standing beside the tracks on the east side. On the west side Cross and Central Avenue run down the sheet and Davis Avenue crosses the top, with Worthington Avenue along the bottom. Between Cross and Central Avenue lies a long, narrow block numbered 48 whose lots are drawn but mostly vacant; the built lots are at the top, along Davis Avenue and Central Avenue, with two and a half storey frame dwellings carrying house numbers from 501 to 515 and 607 to 623. East of the railroad the ground is largely open, laid out in blocks numbered 58 and 59 between Keasbey, Franklyn and Prospect streets with lot lines only, and a few dwellings, a shop and a shed stand along Davis Avenue near the top. Davis Avenue is drawn twice, west and east of the tracks, as a single street crossing them. A pond with its outlet is cut off at the bottom edge. Street widths of 30, 40, 60 and 70 feet and the 6 inch water mains are lettered, the scale of feet and the compass are in the lower corners, and block numbers 21, 22, 34, 35, 37, 49, 61 and 76 refer to adjoining sheets. The header reads Harrison.
notes: Worthington Avenue is now Kingsland Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

Keasbey, Franklyn and Prospect no longer exist (not in OpenStreetMap); the right half of the sheet has no modern junctions, so the placement rests on the Cross, Central and Davis junctions on the western half. Medium confidence.
The railroad is labelled Erie R.R. Newark & Paterson Branch.

sheet-37.description: A district on the Kearny and Harrison boundary, west of Davis Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left. Devon runs down the left edge and Davis Avenue down the right edge, and Tappan, Dukes, Prospect, Franklyn and Keasbey streets cross between them as a set of long parallel blocks. Only the top two blocks are built: Tappan and Dukes streets carry rows of narrow lots with two and two and a half storey frame dwellings and flats, some with stables and coops at the rear, a carpenter's shop with a gas engine, a tin smith and a saloon. A dash-dot line along the south side of Dukes Street marks the boundary between the Town of Kearny and the Town of Harrison. South of it the sheet is largely vacant: blocks numbered 65, 64 and 63 are laid out between Prospect, Franklyn and Keasbey streets with lot lines only at their ends, and a few flats and sheds stand along Devon and North 5th Street at the lower left, including a lumber shed. Street widths of 50, 60 and 70 feet and the 6 inch water mains are lettered along the streets. The compass rose sits in the empty blocks at the lower centre. The header reads Kearny & Harrison, and block numbers 34, 35, 36, 38, 39 and 40 refer to adjoining sheets.
notes: Prospect Street, Franklyn and Keasbey no longer exist here at these places; they are not in the OpenStreetMap network.
Devon Street has two parallel ways in OpenStreetMap near Dukes Street; the northern Devon / Dukes node was excluded.
Devon Street and Davis Avenue are cut by the sheet edge; their centrelines lie at or just beyond it, so three of the four control points are boundary or off-sheet points. Medium to low confidence.
50 ft, north -24. Devon to Davis Av between Tappan and Keasbey; control at the sheet edges (one hand pick just outside the image).

sheet-38.description: A residential district of Kearny near the Harrison line, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. Davis Avenue runs along the bottom of the sheet and Devon Street along the top. Between them four parallel streets run across the sheet: Tappan, Hoyt, Devon Terrace and Pomeroy Avenue, forming three long blocks numbered 1, 2 and 3. Pomeroy Avenue has a small circular park beside its upper end, and Devon Street, Elm Street and Forest Street are cut off by the right edge where they cross it. The blocks are mostly lined with narrow lots; the built frontage is concentrated along Hoyt Street, Tappan Street and Pomeroy Avenue, where two and a half storey frame dwellings and flats stand in rows, with sheds, coops and a small auto shed to the rear. Kearny School No. 8, a large pink-coloured brick building marked as in course of erection, stands in the middle of the block between Hoyt Street and Devon Terrace, and the Central Hose Co. fire station, with a fire alarm box, stands at the Davis Avenue end of Devon Terrace. The 6 and 8 inch water mains and hydrants are lettered along the streets, and street widths of 50, 55, 60 and 70 feet are given. The compass rose is at the lower left, and the blocks 35, 37, 40, 46 and 47 refer to adjoining sheets.
notes: Pomeroy Avenue is now Wilson Avenue in OpenStreetMap (inferred from the position of the modern line through the sheet).
The modern Davis Avenue and Devon Terrace node lies about 12 m from the drawn junction and was excluded.
The second Devon Street and Wilson Avenue node in OpenStreetMap (a parallel way) was excluded.
50 ft, north +60. Tappan to Pomeroy (Wilson Avenue), Devon to Davis Av.

sheet-39.description: Central Kearny at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right of the sheet. The map covers a rectangle of three blocks between Maple Street at the top and Devon Street at the bottom, with Chestnut Street between them and Kearny Avenue crossing the upper part. Johnston Avenue bounds it on the left and Woodland Avenue on the right. The Erie Railroad (Newark and Paterson Branch) runs down the left side of the sheet with the town boundary of Harrison and Kearny beside it, and the boundary of Kearny and Harrison is also drawn along Devon Street at the bottom, labelled North 5th Street on the Harrison side. The district is closely built with frame dwellings, flats and stores. Public buildings along Kearny Avenue include the Kearny Public School, Kearny Hose Co. No. 2 and Truck Co. No. 2, the Town Hall with its hose tower, the Knox Presbyterian Church and its chapel. A wagon maker's shop, a coal yard and a print shop stand on the long block between Johnston Avenue and the railroad at the left. Block numbers 1 to 4 are printed in the blocks, lot numbers along the frontages, and street widths of 50, 60 and 80 feet at the corners. Water mains of the Suburban Water Company run along Kearny Avenue. The margins repeat the numbers of the adjoining sheets (42, 32, 33, 34, 37 and 40); the areas beyond Maple and Devon Streets are blank here and belong to those sheets. Keasbey, Franklyn and Prospect Streets are lettered in the blank area at the bottom.

sheet-40.description: Part of central Kearny drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper left of the sheet (the compass at lower left points to the upper left). Four streets run up the sheet: Maple on the left, Kearny Avenue (80 feet wide) beside it, Chestnut, and Devon on the right, where the Kearny and Harrison town boundary and North 5th Street are lettered. They are crossed by Hoyt Street at the top, Dukes Street in the middle, and Rose Street at the lower left. The left half of the sheet is a residential district of long, narrow lots with frame dwellings, many still vacant, along Maple Street and Kearny Avenue. The block between Kearny Avenue and Chestnut Street holds St. Cecilia's Roman Catholic Church, its rectory and parochial school at the top, and a wheelwright and carriage maker, paint shop and small stores below. Below Dukes Street the ground is largely vacant: a large block numbered 4 lies empty apart from a club house, bounded below by Woodland Avenue, which crosses the sheet at a slant with a row of small dwellings, a saloon, blacksmith shops and tin shops along its north side. A saloon and dwellings also stand at the lower left on Maple Street. Dashed lines mark the 6, 20 and 30 inch water mains of the Suburban Water Company on Kearny Avenue and the cross streets. Block numbers 0 to 5 are printed in the blocks and street widths of 45 to 80 feet at the corners. The corners of the sheet show the numbers of neighbouring sheets (46 above, 42, 38, 37 and 39).

sheet-41.description: The Passaic River frontage of Kearny drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper left. Passaic Avenue runs down the middle of the sheet beside the river, with the river bank and water along the left edge. Marshall Street crosses the top, Clark and Sherman Avenue run down the right side, Belgrove Drive sweeps across the lower half, and Johnston Avenue forms the bottom of the built-up area with Lincoln Avenue running between Belgrove Drive and Johnston Avenue. The Erie Railroad (Newark and Paterson Branch) crosses the foot of the sheet. The sheet is dominated by the works of Marshall and Company, linen thread and twines, a mutual risk plant of sprinklered mill buildings in brick and frame east of Passaic Avenue, with storage buildings, drying sheds, a hemp store, engine and boiler rooms and a tunnel under the avenue to the storage yard on the river side. On the river side Passaic Avenue serves the Barber Asphalt Paving Company works, with its melting and mixing houses and a wagon shed, and further down the Stanley Roofing and Paving Company and the Keystone Cement and Construction Company, a patent stone works. At lower right stand the Business Men's Hygeia Ice Company plant and blocks of flats and tenements along Lincoln Avenue, Johnston Avenue and Sherman Avenue. Between the works and Belgrove Drive the large block is vacant. Water mains and fire hydrants are marked, and block numbers 1 to 3 are printed. The numbers of adjoining sheets (44, 42 and 31) are shown at the edges.

sheet-42.description: A residential strip of Kearny drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper left. Johnston Avenue crosses the bottom of the sheet from Sherman Avenue at the left to Maple Street at the right, and Woodland Avenue crosses the upper middle. Between them four streets run up the sheet and fan slightly apart: Sherman Avenue, Grant Avenue, John, Highland Avenue and Maple. Belgrove Drive curves in from the upper left to meet Grant Avenue and Woodland Avenue; its wide, curved sweep is drawn through the lower left, where it cuts across the blocks. Clark runs down the left edge. The blocks between Johnston Avenue and Woodland Avenue are lined with narrow lots of frame dwellings, flats and some three-storey tenements, most densely along John Street, Highland Avenue and Maple Street, with a livery stable on the block between Highland Avenue and Maple Street, a print shop on John Street and a mission hall and saloons along Johnston Avenue. At the lower left the Kearny Hat Works, manufacturers of ladies hats, stands on the Sherman Avenue block among tenements and flats. A row of seven new dwellings lines the north side of Woodland Avenue at the right. The area above Woodland Avenue (block 5) and the large area at the upper left are vacant. Block numbers 1 to 6 are printed in the blocks. Neighbouring sheet numbers 44, 41, 40, 39, 31 and 32 appear at the edges, and the compass shows north to the upper left.

sheet-43-1.description: The Nairn Linoleum Company works on the Passaic River side of Kearny, drawn at 60 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper left. Passaic Avenue bounds the works on the left, Bergen Avenue crosses the top at a slant, Hillside Avenue forms the right boundary and Nairn Avenue runs along the bottom, with Belgrove Drive and Pomeroy Avenue at the right edge. The works fill the large central tract with brick, fireproof mills numbered 1 to 18 and lettered sections, most fitted with automatic sprinklers: the oil cloth plant and drying rooms at the top (Mill No. 10), the linoleum plant and printing rooms with trimming and drying rooms (Mill No. 3), Mill No. 2 and its callender rooms, Mill Nos. 5, 7, 8 and 14 with their cement rooms and engine houses, Mill No. 9 with its generator and engine room, Mill No. 12 and Mill No. 13A and 13B near the foot, together with a reservoir, pump house, storage sheds and oil tanks. Water pipes, hydrants and tanks are traced through the grounds. A printed report in the left margin details The Nairn Linoleum Co. watchmen, fire pails, hose carts and sprinkler systems. At the left a storage shed and concrete mixing and grinding buildings stand on the river side of Passaic Avenue, and at the lower left a building used for storage of machinery by The Clark Thread Co., not in operation. Along the right side a block of long narrow lots between Hillside Avenue and Belgrove Drive holds only a few flats and dwellings. The Passaic River appears at the upper left. An inset boxed by a heavy line at the upper right (automatic railway and coal pile) belongs to another part and is not covered here.
notes: Bergen Avenue, Passaic Avenue and Belgrove Drive keep their names today; Hillside Avenue and Nairn Avenue no longer exist, and the Nairn works site is now largely beneath the Interstate 280 corridor.

sheet-44.description: A sparsely built strip of Kearny along the Passaic River, drawn at 60 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper left. Passaic Avenue runs down the left of the middle of the sheet, with the winding Passaic River and its banks occupying the left third. Marshall Street crosses the foot, Mc Nary crosses the middle, Nairn Avenue runs across the upper right, and Watts and Clark run down between them, with Belgrove Drive and Hillside Avenue at the right. The upper part belongs to The Nairn Linoleum Co. (see Sheet 43): Mill No. 16 stands in the grounds with Mill No. 17 being built and Mill No. 18 to be built, and the tops of the Mill 12 and Mill 13 buildings appear along the top edge. A small row of dwellings stands at the right on lots lettered G to K. Between Mc Nary and Marshall Streets lie two long blocks of narrow lots divided by Watts, nearly all vacant: a double row of about twenty lots between Watts and Clark has about a dozen frame dwellings, and a row of flats, a store and a shed stand at the south end of the block beside Passaic Avenue. Block numbers 1 to 5 are printed. The adjoining sheets 43, 41 and 42 are named at the edges, and the compass at lower left shows north toward the upper left.

sheet-45.description: A mostly vacant residential tract in the north of Kearny, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left of the sheet. Bergen Avenue, 70 feet wide, runs across the top edge, with only its southern frontage shown. Belgrove Drive on the left edge, Brighton Avenue, Highland Avenue and the narrower Windsor (50 feet) run down the sheet and are cut by Pomeroy Avenue, 60 feet wide, about three fifths of the way down. The long, narrow house lots between the avenues are laid out and numbered but are almost all unbuilt; the few frame dwellings stand along Bergen Avenue and on the Brighton Avenue blocks, and a short row of flats, some of them brick-fronted and some with stores, stands along Pomeroy Avenue and beside Belgrove Drive. An elongated pond, lettered as such, lies between Highland Avenue and Windsor, extending from near Bergen Avenue down to Pomeroy Avenue. The lower part of the sheet, south of Pomeroy Avenue, is mainly blank lots except for the grounds of the Sisters of Charity Italian Protectory, shown with its chapel, dormitories and school rooms, wood sheds and a greenhouse, with a note on heating, lighting and fire extinguishers. Six and eight inch water mains and hydrants are marked in the streets, and street widths are lettered in feet. The sheet is headed Kearny and Harrison & Kearny, N.J.; the margin carries the sheet number and references to neighbouring sheets (49 above, 43 to the left and 46 to the right), and a scale of feet at the foot.

sheet-46.description: The built-up centre of Kearny along Kearny Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left of the sheet. Bergen Avenue runs across the top edge, where a block holding a drug store stands at its corner with Kearny Avenue. Kearny Avenue, 80 feet wide and carrying the 20 inch and 30 inch mains of the Suburban Water Company, crosses the sheet from top to bottom. Maple on its west and Chestnut and Devon Pl. on its east run parallel to it, and Windsor lies along the left edge. Boyd and Pomeroy Avenue cut across at about a third and two thirds of the way down, and Hoyt closes the sheet at the bottom. Dwellings, many of them two and a half storey frame houses with sheds and coops at the rear, fill the Kearny Avenue frontage and the blocks east of it, with rows of flats, some brick-fronted, along the Pomeroy Avenue frontage on the sheet's left edge and east of Chestnut. Beula M.E. Church stands on the west side of Maple, a lumber shed and carpenter's shop stand between Maple and Kearny Avenue, and flats and dwellings line Kearny Avenue and the east side of the sheet toward Bergen Avenue. Large parts of the Windsor block on the left remain unbuilt lots. Water pipes, hydrants and street widths in feet are lettered throughout. A compass rose with a north arrow stands at upper right, and sheet references 49, 50, 45, 47, 40 and 38 are printed around the margins. sheet-47.description: A residential district of Kearny between Pomeroy Avenue on the left and Bergen Avenue on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the streets running across the page and north toward the upper right of the sheet. Chestnut runs along the top edge, followed by Devon Pl. (a 20 foot street) and Devon, Elm, Forest and Davis Av., which closes the sheet at the bottom. Boyd, a 50 foot street, joins Chestnut to Devon in the upper left, and a small circular park lies beside Pomeroy Avenue at the upper left. The long blocks are cut into narrow deep lots. The frontages along Devon and Elm, and the Bergen Avenue end of Chestnut, carry rows of two and a half storey frame dwellings and several flats; the blocks between Elm and Davis Av. are largely vacant except near Bergen Avenue, where the Kearny Union Sunday School, with a note on its heating and lights, stands at the corner of Davis Av. sheet-48.description: A sparsely built residential tract in Kearny between Bergen Av. on the left and Garfield Av. on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the streets running across the page and north toward the upper right of the sheet. Elm runs along the top, followed by Forest, Davis and, at the foot of the sheet, Ivy, each 55 to 70 feet wide, with Garfield Av. 60 feet wide on the right. The long blocks between Elm and Davis are divided into deep narrow lots, almost all vacant; a few frame dwellings with outbuildings stand on the Elm and Forest frontages and along the north side of Davis, where a row of dwellings faces the street. sheet-49.description: A largely open tract in the north of Kearny between Bergen Av. on the left and Afton on the right, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the streets running across the page and north toward the upper right of the sheet. Belgrove Drive runs along the top, followed by Brighton Av., Highland Av., Windsor Av. and, at the foot of the sheet, Maple. The upper block between Belgrove Drive and Brighton Av. is a single large parcel of open ground holding a circular reservoir and a water tank (lettered W. Tank, 30 feet above grade), with a few buildings along its Afton end. The three blocks below are divided into long narrow lots, almost all vacant. Dwellings are concentrated in a row of eight facing Bergen Av. on the Brighton and Highland block, in a group at the Afton end of the Highland block (some of them coloured as brick), and in scattered frame houses along Windsor Av. and Maple. sheet-50.description: A residential district of central Kearny drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right of the sheet. The part covers four long blocks between Bergen Avenue on the west and Garfield Avenue (Afton Street north of Kearny Avenue) on the east, running from Maple Street at the top through Kearny Avenue, Chestnut Street and Devon Street to Elm Street at the bottom. Kearny Avenue, the town's main north-south artery, crosses the upper third of the sheet. The blocks are laid out in narrow, deep house lots, most of them still vacant in 1907; the built lots carry frame dwellings, many with rear sheds and stables, concentrated along Kearny Avenue, the Devon Street frontage and the Bergen Avenue corners. The most notable building is the Essex Pearl Button Company, a brick works with a finishing room, machine shop, polishing and carding departments and a described power and fire-protection layout, on the block east of Devon Street. A row of flats and a few small outbuildings stand near it, and a fire alarm box is marked at the top right. Neighbouring sheets are 70 to the left, 74 to the right, 71 below on Laurel Avenue and 69 below left. Streets are marked 60 feet wide.

sheet-74.description: Sheet 74 is the eastern edge of the Arlington part of Kearny, at 50 feet to an inch, turned like sheet 73 so that north points toward the upper left. Elm Street runs down the left edge, Forest Street down the left third and Davis Avenue up from the bottom; Schuyler Avenue runs down the right side, slanting to the right at the bottom. Stuyvesant Avenue is at the top, Prospect Place crosses the upper part, Stewart Avenue the middle, Magnolia Avenue below it and Laurel Avenue along the bottom edge. The blocks at the top and left have rows of frame dwellings, a row of flats on Elm Street, and a small group of houses along Prospect Place. The right and lower parts are given over to florists and market gardens: G. Marti, florist, with greenhouses at the corner of Stewart Avenue and Schuyler Avenue, a larger range of greenhouses with a heated boiler building to the south, and Silas Van Amburgh, florist and gardener, with long greenhouses and a boiler pit in the lower block. At the top right Salmond Brothers Company, general contractors, has a yard with sheds. Streets are marked 60 feet wide with 6 inch water pipe. Adjoining sheets named are 73 to the left and 72 below. A library stamp and the scale of feet appear at the lower right.
notes: The sheet is turned: fitted rotation about -35 degrees.
Forest Street / Laurel Avenue and Davis Avenue / Laurel Avenue on the bottom edge were hand-picked from the drawn street edges (centre 30 feet beyond the block line).

sheet-75-1.description: The top strip and right part of sheet 75, in the north of Kearny, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left and bounded on the left by the heavy dividing line of the sheet. Bergen Av., 70 feet wide, runs along the bottom of the part with a row of dwellings on its north frontage, and meets Ivy, Worthington Av. (Kingsland Av.) and Schuyler Av. at the foot of the sheet. Ivy runs up the middle of the part; Schuyler Av., 50 feet wide, runs up the right side on a slight diagonal. Most of the ground is open lots and farm land. Swain Bro's Diary Farm, with large barns and sheds, stands in the top strip, and the Kearny Iron Fence Co., with a gas engine and a note on its power and lights, stands on the Ivy block, together with scattered frame dwellings, hen houses and outbuildings. A block of long narrow lots lies between Ivy and Schuyler Av. Water pipes of 6 inches and hydrants are marked in the streets, a fire alarm box stands near the corner of Bergen Av. and Schuyler Av., and widths are lettered. A compass rose and north arrow stand at the right, and a scale of feet at the foot. The sheet is headed Kearny, and a Library of Congress duplicate stamp lies in the lower left.
notes: Bergen Av. is Bergen Avenue, Ivy is Ivy Street, Schuyler Av. is Schuyler Avenue and Worthington Av. (Kingsland Av.) is Kingsland Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-75-2.description: The lower left part of sheet 75, in the north of Kearny, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north toward the upper left and divided from the rest of the sheet by a heavy line along its top and right sides. Bergen Av., 60 to 70 feet wide, crosses the top of the part on a diagonal; Ivy St. ends against it at the far left edge. Worthington (Kingsland) Av., 60 feet wide, runs from Bergen Av. toward the lower left, and Schuyler Av., 50 feet wide, runs straight down the right side of the part. South of Bergen Av. the blocks are cut into narrow deep lots, mostly unbuilt. A few frame dwellings stand on the Bergen Av. frontage, and the block between Worthington (Kingsland) Av. and Schuyler Av. holds Kearny Public School No. 1, lettered Kearny Public Shool No. 1 with a note on its heating and extinguishers, and further down a wood sawing shop, a small group of flats and some sheds. A fire alarm box stands at the corner of Bergen Av. and Schuyler Av., with 6 inch water pipes and hydrants in the streets. The lower half of the part is blank apart from a compass rose and north arrow, a scale of feet and a Library of Congress duplicate stamp. The other part of the sheet draws the ground on the other side of Bergen Av. at a different orientation.
notes: Worthington (Kingsland) Av. is Kingsland Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Bergen Av. is Bergen Avenue, Schuyler Av. is Schuyler Avenue and Ivy St. is Ivy Street.

sheet-76.description: A district on the Harrison and Kearny boundary drawn at 50 feet to an inch, with north toward the upper right. Schuyler Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the right, meeting Dukes Street and Tappan Street, which run up the sheet in parallel. Essex Avenue runs across the lower right and Sandford Avenue across the bottom, with Watkins Street between them at the lower left. A large pond with a winding shore fills the upper left; the line of the Town of Harrison and the Town of Kearny runs down through it. West of the pond Franklyn and Prospect streets and Worthington Avenue are laid out as blocks numbered 56 and 57, with no buildings, and the tracks of the Erie Railroad's Newark and Paterson Branch run down the left edge. The built area is east of Dukes Street. Along Schuyler Avenue and Tappan Street stand frame dwellings, flats and sheds, a fire alarm box at the Tappan Street corner, and two industrial premises: the David Essex Machine Shop with a steam engine, and A. H. Workman's wire cloth weaving works, run by hand power with electric lights and no fire apparatus. At the lower left J. G. Perry, florist, has a range of greenhouses on Watkins Street. The blocks above Tappan and Dukes streets are long strips of narrow lots, mostly vacant. The header reads Harrison & Kearny, the compass rose is at the top left, and block numbers 22, 23, 35, 36 and 0 refer to adjoining sheets.
notes: Sandford Avenue is now Sanford Avenue and Essex Avenue is now Essex Place in OpenStreetMap.
Franklyn, Prospect, Watkins and Worthington Avenue (here a street at the top of the sheet) are not in the OpenStreetMap network at these places.
The railroad at the left edge is labelled Erie R.R. Newark & Paterson Branch.
